claim: .NET 10 emits OpenAPI 3.1 by default (JSON Schema draft 2020-12); the version is switchable via OpenApiOptions.OpenApiVersion, and ProducesProblem/ProducesValidationProblem/TypedResults.Problem add the ProblemDetails response metadata.
quote: Starting in .NET 11, the default OpenAPI version for generated documents is 3.2. In .NET 10, the default is 3.1. To change the version, explicitly set the OpenApiVersion property of the OpenApiOptions

claim: .NET 10 emits numeric properties as a string|integer union with a regex pattern, which poisons every generated TypeScript client; the fix is JsonNumberHandling.Strict or a schema transformer.
quote: "type": ["integer", "string"], "pattern": "^-?(?:0|[1-9]\\d*)$", "format": "int32" ... This causes client code generators for TypeScript and other platforms to struggle, since the schema suggests a value could be either a number or a string

claim: .NET 10's generated ProblemDetails schema declares only the five RFC 7807 fields and no additionalProperties, so ProblemDetails extensions are invisible to any generator; the issue was closed as answered rather than fixed.
quote: "ProblemDetails": { "type": "object", "properties": { "type": {...}, "title": {...}, "status": {...}, "detail": {...}, "instance": {...} } }

claim: TanStack Query's maintainer argues queryOptions is the abstraction to reach for first and that a wrapper hook per endpoint is no longer the default advice.
quote: There's nothing wrong with calling useQuery in your component directly ... Separating QueryKey from QueryFunction was a mistake

claim: queryOptions is TanStack Query v5's official type-safe helper for sharing a query definition between hooks and imperative QueryClient methods.
Orval's react-query mode generates one custom hook per operation plus a getXQueryKey() function and the bare fetcher.
quote: export const useShowPetById = <TData = AsyncReturnType<typeof showPetById>, TError = Error,>(petId: string, options?: { query?: UseQueryOptions<...>; axios?: AxiosRequestConfig; },)

claim: Orval hand-rolls its option objects instead of calling TanStack's queryOptions helper; the generated suspense option functions are consequently unusable in useSuspenseQuery/useSuspenseQueries. Still open.
quote: generated `getUse*SuspenseQueryOptions()` are not usable in `useSuspenseQuery` / `useSuspenseQueries` in the current version

claim: Orval types the TError channel of its generated hooks through an ErrorType alias exported from the custom mutator.
quote: export type ErrorType<Error> = AxiosError<Error>;

claim: Orval's mock: true generates MSW handlers and Faker data alongside the client — the feature no rival matches.
CVE-2026-24132 (CVSS 7.7): a malicious OpenAPI document can inject arbitrary TypeScript into Orval's generated mock files; fixed in 7.20.0 and 8.0.3.
quote: Orval generates type-safe JS clients (TypeScript) from any valid OpenAPI v3 or Swagger v2 specification. Versions 7.19.0 and below and 8.0.0-rc.0 through 8.0.2 allow untrusted OpenAPI specifications to inject arbitrary TypeScript/JavaScript into generated mock files via the const keyword on schema

claim: Orval reads OpenAPI 3.1 type arrays and emits the resulting `| null` unions, so .NET 10's 3.1 nullability lands correctly.
Hey API's TanStack Query plugin emits queryOptions, infiniteQueryOptions, mutationOptions and queryKey functions rather than hooks.
quote: The generated query functions follow the naming convention of SDK functions and by default append `Options`, e.g., `getPetByIdOptions()`.

claim: Hey API's generated output imports TanStack's real queryOptions helper and calls the SDK with throwOnError: true, so the options objects are first-class TanStack citizens.
quote: import { type DefaultError, queryOptions, type UseMutationOptions } from '@tanstack/react-query';

claim: Hey API resolves the TError generic to the operation's generated error type when the spec declares error responses, falling back to DefaultError only when it declares none.
quote: const symbolError = symbolErrorType || plugin.imports.DefaultError;

claim: Hey API's throwOnError once stringified the error body into Error.message, discarding the typed ProblemDetails at runtime; closed by PR #1098.
quote: The throwOnError option makes sense - this is what tanstack-query expects when we get a 300+ status code. However, how do we then leverage the types provided by the OpenAPI spec if everything is wrapped as a string in Error.message?

claim: Hey API (@hey-api/openapi-ts) is MIT-licensed, ships 20+ plugins, and is used by Vercel, PayPal and AWS.
Hey API's hosted Platform is optional — input accepts a local file or URL just as well as a hey-api/* registry reference.
quote: input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev

claim: openapi-typescript supports OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 and emits runtime-free types only.
quote: ✅ Supports OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 (including advanced features like discriminators)

claim: openapi-fetch is a 6 kB fetch wrapper that returns a { data, error } discriminated union, both sides typed from the spec.
quote:
data, // only present if 2XX response
error, // only present if 4XX or 5XX response

claim: openapi-react-query is a ~1 kB runtime wrapper over TanStack Query — not a generator — exposing queryOptions, useQuery, useSuspenseQuery, useInfiniteQuery and useMutation.

openapi-react-query's queryFn throws the parsed error body, and its query keys are branded DataTag<key, data, error> — so useQuery().error and queryClient.setQueryData() are both typed straight from the spec.
Kiota's own README marks TypeScript/JavaScript as in preview (🛠️) across generation, abstractions, serialization and HTTP.
Kiota's maturity ladder: Stable means production API clients; Preview means near-stable but not used for production clients; Experimental means some features might not work at all.
quote: Preview: Kiota is at or near the level of stable but isn't being used to generate production API clients.

claim: Kiota generates a fluent request-builder client (client.posts.byPostId(id).get()) whose models are all-optional, and requires a Kiota-specific request adapter and auth provider.
quote: const specificPost = await client.posts.byPostId(specificPostId).get();

claim: Kiota ships as a binary download, a Docker image or a .NET global tool — there is no npm distribution, so a Node/Nx CI job must install a second toolchain.
quote: dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota

claim: The TypeScript runtime libraries Kiota's generated clients depend on sit in a repo with 61 stars.
Nx's sync generators plus `nx sync:check` give a first-class way to fail CI when a generated artifact has drifted from its source.
quote: Check that no changes are required after running all sync generators.

@hey-api/openapi-ts drew 2.88M npm downloads in the week of 5-11 Jul 2026; orval drew 1.29M and @microsoft/kiota-bundle 47.9k.
